trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to Eixample. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk along Passeig de Gràcia to spot the iconic facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside — free to admire from the street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample neighbourhood on foot. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for tapas bar hopping. Try pintxos and a glass of house wine at a local bar. Afterwards, stroll through the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia for a gentle introduction to Barcelona's nightlife scene without overspending on night one.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo (sandwich) from a Mercadona supermarket near the hotel (€2–4) after check-in
meals.dinner: Bar Calders or similar neighbourhood tapas bar in Eixample — order house wine and 3–4 pintxos (€10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival — it covers all metro and bus trips and will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot (30°C+), so carry a water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sagrada Família first thing when it opens (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry, or €36 with tower access — worth it for architecture lovers). Spend 1.5–2 hours marvelling at Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, both interior and exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (Metro L3 to Vallcarca or bus 24). The Monumental Zone requires a ticket (€10, book online), but the surrounding park terraces and streets are free and offer stunning city views. Spend 2 hours exploring. Afterwards, walk downhill through the Gràcia neighbourhood — browse its charming plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, which are free and full of local life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore the Gayxample area (around Carrer del Consell de Cent) known for vibrant bars and affordable cocktail happy hours. Many bars offer 2-for-1 drinks before 21:00. This is a great low-cost introduction to Barcelona's nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and tostada con tomate (toast with tomato) at a local café near the hotel (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or Gràcia — typically includes starter, main, dessert, and drink (€12–14)
meals.dinner: Supermercat (supermarket) picnic supplies — bread, jamón, cheese, olives, and local beer from Lidl or Mercadona (€6–8), enjoyed in a nearby plaza

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online to save time and guarantee entry. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking and hills today.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) via metro. Explore the medieval labyrinth of streets for free — highlights include the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30), Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the Roman Temple of Augustus (free entry). Allow 2–3 hours to wander and photograph the architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to El Born neighbourhood, adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, stunning Gothic interior). Explore the Mercat de Santa Caterina (free to browse, cheaper than La Boqueria). Then head to La Barceloneta beach (15-minute walk) for a swim and relaxation — completely free. Rent a sun lounger if desired (€5–8) or simply use your towel on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's famous nightlife. Pre-drink at a rooftop bar in El Born (many offer affordable happy hours until 22:00). Head to Razzmatazz or Sala Apolo (entry €10–15 with a drink included if you arrive before midnight). Both are iconic Barcelona clubs beloved for their architecture and music variety. Alternatively, explore free street performances and bars around Plaça Reial.

meals.breakfast: Granja M. Viader or any local granja café in the Gothic Quarter — hot chocolate and a croissant (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh produce and snacks from Mercat de Santa Caterina — grab fruit, a slice of tortilla española, and olives (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Early dinner at a menú del día restaurant in El Born before heading out — look for chalkboard specials (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your belongings secure in the Gothic Quarter — it is a tourist-heavy area with pickpocket activity. Clubs in Barcelona typically don't fill up until 01:00–02:00 AM, so there's no need to rush.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — one of the most breathtaking Modernista buildings in the world by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours cost €22 but are worth every cent for architecture lovers. Book in advance. Alternatively, attend a morning concert for as little as €15–18 if one is scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Metro L3 to Poble Sec and explore Montjuïc hill. Ride the Funicular de Montjuïc (included in T-Casual card) to the top. Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50). Walk to the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for panoramic views of the entire city and port. The Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (€5) is nearby and a must-see for architecture fans — a minimalist icon.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Eixample for a neighbourhood dinner and bar crawl. Walk along Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec (nearby) — the famous pintxos street where most bites cost just €1–2 each. Afterwards, explore Eixample's cocktail bar scene — Dry Martini or Milano are legendary but pricier; opt for neighbourhood cocktail bars charging €7–9 per drink.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café near Palau de la Música — café amb llet and a pastry (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc — buy supplies from a local supermarket before heading up (€5–7)
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl in Poble Sec — fill up on pintxos and a cold beer (€10–14 total)

day_by_day.notes: The Montjuïc Magic Fountain show runs on Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer (free) — check the schedule and consider staying for it before heading to the bar crawl.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning at the Eixample block known as La Manzana de la Discordia on Passeig de Gràcia — three rival Modernista buildings side by side. Casa Lleó Morera (free exterior), Casa Amatller (exterior free, tours from €12), and Casa Batlló (€29–35, worth it for architecture lovers — book online). If budget is tight, admire all three from the street for free and save funds for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) on Montjuïc — entry is €12 but free on the first Sunday of the month and after 15:00 on Saturdays. The building itself (the Palau Nacional) is a stunning piece of architecture. Alternatively, do a final souvenir shopping sweep at El Corte Inglés or local shops on Passeig de Gràcia. Head back to the hotel, pack, and check out.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final farewell dinner in Eixample. Try a classic Catalan restaurant offering escalivada, pa amb tomàquet, and crema catalana. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 to the airport for your departure.

meals.breakfast: Final café breakfast near the hotel — tostada con tomate, fresh orange juice, and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Menú del día near MNAC or a packed lunch from the supermarket (€8–13)
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in Eixample — look for a set dinner menu (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for travel to the airport and check-in. Store luggage at the hotel if check-out is before your flight. Total estimated budget for 5 days excluding flights and accommodation: €150–200 per person, covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Barcelona Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Park Güell Sunrise Visit & Gracia Brunch
experiences.description: Beat the crowds with an early morning visit to Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park, enjoying the mosaic terraces and sweeping city views at golden hour. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a leisurely brunch at a local café among tree-lined plazas.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Time is needed for baggage claim, airport transfer, and hotel check-in at Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: After checking in and freshening up, take a leisurely self-guided stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to get your bearings. Admire the exteriors of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the street — a perfect free introduction to Gaudí's genius right from your Eixample doorstep. Pop into any local pharmacy or supermarket to grab essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's rhythm with a relaxed evening in Eixample. Explore the 'Gayxample' neighbourhood streets and enjoy your first taste of local nightlife with vermouth and pintxos at a neighbourhood bar before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution for tapas and montaditos at mid-range prices (€15–20 per person). Arrive before 14:30 to avoid long waits.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda on Carrer de Sepúlveda — a cosy, unpretentious wine bar and restaurant serving traditional Catalan dishes. Budget around €25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Eixample is extremely walkable and safe, so a casual neighbourhood wander is the perfect low-key introduction. Book all ticketed experiences in advance online to avoid sold-out situations in peak August.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Start the day with the crown jewel of Barcelona architecture. Your skip-the-line guided tour (pre-booked) allows a deep dive into Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the breathtaking interior forest of columns, and optionally ascending a tower for panoramic views. Allow 2–2.5 hours. The basilica is a short taxi or metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gaudí Architecture Walking Tour — Seamlessly continue your architectural immersion with a guided walking tour covering Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Palau Güell. Your Eixample hotel puts you within walking distance of the first two stops. The tour reveals the symbolism and innovation behind each façade and interior. Finish around 17:00 and rest briefly at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Gothic Quarter Night Walk & Tapas Crawl — As the August heat softens after sunset, join the atmospheric evening tour through the medieval lanes of the Gothic Quarter. Wind through Roman ruins, hidden plazas, and candlelit alleys while sampling local tapas and cava at curated stops. This is Barcelona's historic soul after dark.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café on Carrer del Parlament — a beloved brunch spot with excellent coffee, avocado toast, and eggs. Budget €10–15. Arrive by 08:30 before the queue builds.
meals.lunch: Quick and satisfying lunch near Sagrada Família — try La Pepita Gràcia on Carrer de Còrsega for creative montaditos and fresh juices. Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Gothic Quarter Tapas Crawl experience. Expect a variety of pintxos, patatas bravas, jamón, and local wine across multiple stops.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak tourist season — Sagrada Família and Casa Batlló sell out weeks in advance. Confirm all bookings before departure. Wear comfortable walking shoes; the Gothic Quarter's cobblestones are uneven. Carry a small water bottle — August temperatures in Barcelona regularly exceed 30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell Sunrise Visit & Gràcia Brunch — Set your alarm early for this magical experience. Arrive at Park Güell just after sunrise (approximately 06:30–07:00 in August) to enjoy Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park bathed in golden light with minimal crowds. Explore the mosaic terraces, the iconic dragon staircase, and the Monumental Zone before the timed-entry rush begins. Take in sweeping views over Barcelona toward the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: After brunch in Gràcia, return to the hotel for a midday rest during the hottest hours. Then head to the Eixample neighbourhood for a self-guided interior design and modernisme walk — visit the Bloc de la Discòrdia (Block of Discord) on Passeig de Gràcia, where Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera stand alongside Casa Batlló. Browse independent boutiques and concept stores in the neighbourhood at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Clubbing on Carrer de Parlament & Poble Sec — Begin the night with craft cocktails at a rooftop bar in Poble Sec, enjoying sunset views over the city. Progress through the vibrant bar scene on Carrer de Parlament before heading to a club for Barcelona's legendary late-night scene. Barcelona nightlife doesn't peak until midnight–02:00, so pace yourself.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack before heading to Park Güell — prepare a takeaway coffee and pastry the evening before, or stop at a 24-hour bakery near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Gràcia Brunch (part of the Park Güell experience) — La Pepita or Bar Calders in Gràcia/Poble Sec for a leisurely brunch with fresh orange juice, eggs, and pa amb tomàquet. Budget €12–18.
meals.dinner: Bodega 1900 on Carrer de Tamarit in Poble Sec — Albert Adrià's sophisticated take on classic vermouth-bar culture. Elevated tapas in a beautiful vintage setting. Budget €35–45 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed-entry tickets for the Monumental Zone must be booked online in advance — they sell out quickly in August. The early morning visit means the park is at its most peaceful and photogenic. If the nightlife evening runs very late, plan for a slower start on Day 4.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed late start to recover from the previous night. Take a slow morning walk through the Eixample neighbourhood, exploring the famous 'Superblocks' (Superilles) urban project and the Sant Antoni market area. Visit the Mercat de Sant Antoni — a beautifully restored iron market hall — to browse fresh produce, local cheeses, and artisan goods. Perfect for picking up picnic supplies or simply soaking in local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta beach for an afternoon of sun and sea — a well-deserved mid-trip rest. Rent a sunbed and parasol, take a swim in the Mediterranean, and explore the beachfront promenade. Alternatively, visit the El Born neighbourhood for its eclectic mix of medieval architecture, independent galleries, and the impressive ruins of the Mercat de Santa Caterina. Browse boutiques and visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, a stunning Gothic church.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner and drinks in El Born or La Barceloneta, followed by a nightcap along the waterfront. Enjoy the cooler evening air with a walk along the Port Olímpic marina, watching yachts and the city lights reflect on the water. An earlier, more relaxed evening to recharge before the final full day.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at home base — pick up fresh pastries, fruit, and coffee from a local Eixample bakery such as Forn de Sant Jaume or a neighbourhood café. Budget €5–8.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc de la Ciutadella using market finds from Sant Antoni, or grab a fresh seafood lunch at La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrive early — they close when food runs out). Budget €15–20.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary, atmospheric cava bar and tapas restaurant with marble tables and walls lined with wine bottles. Order the house cava and anchovies. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is intentionally paced as a recovery and exploration day after the high-activity Days 2 and 3. Barceloneta can be extremely crowded in August — arrive early for a good spot or opt for the quieter Bogatell or Mar Bella beaches slightly further along the coast. El Born is best explored in the afternoon when shops open after siesta.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk through the Eixample to revisit any favourite spots or tick off anything missed. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies on Carrer d'Aragó — a converted modernista publishing house turned contemporary art museum, just steps from the hotel. A compact, rewarding cultural experience showcasing Barcelona's art scene beyond Gaudí. Allow 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping along Passeig de Gràcia and the surrounding streets. Pick up quality local gifts — olive oils, cava, artisan ceramics, or design items from the many concept stores in Eixample. Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Take a final stroll through the neighbourhood, pausing at a favourite café for one last cortado.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — a celebratory final meal to close out the trip. Depending on departure time, enjoy a long, leisurely dinner in true Spanish style, embracing the late dining culture one final time.

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café on Carrer de Llúria — a bright, welcoming spot in Eixample with excellent specialty coffee, avocado toast, and homemade cakes. Budget €10–15. A perfect final morning treat.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snack while shopping — grab a bocadillo from a local deli or a fresh juice and empanada from a neighbourhood bakery. Budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Carrer de Londres — a beloved Eixample restaurant with outstanding Neapolitan-style pizza and natural wines in a relaxed, stylish setting. A fun, satisfying farewell meal. Budget €25–35 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics in advance — if flying out on the 20th, enjoy a full relaxed evening. If departing late on the 19th, adjust the dinner reservation accordingly. The Eixample location offers excellent metro and taxi access to Barcelona El Prat Airport (T1 and T2). Allow at least 90 minutes for airport transfer and check-in during August peak season. Consider storing luggage at the hotel until dinner if checkout is earlier than your flight.

trip_options.title: Premium Barcelona Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from El Prat Airport to your boutique hotel in Eixample. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gaudí Architecture Walking Tour: Begin your Barcelona experience with a private guided walking tour of the Eixample district's architectural crown jewels — Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera), both a short stroll from your hotel. Your expert guide reveals the symbolism and genius behind Gaudí's organic facades, rooftop warriors, and surrealist interiors. Upgrade to include priority access to Casa Batlló's Magic Nights rooftop for an unforgettable late-afternoon perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Gothic Quarter Night Walk & Tapas Crawl: As the sun sets and Barcelona awakens, join a curated private night walk through the labyrinthine medieval lanes of the Gothic Quarter. Visit hidden plazas, Roman ruins, and candlelit tapas bars. Enjoy premium pintxos, jamón ibérico de bellota, and aged Manchego paired with fine Catalan wines at select stops along the route.

meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda — a beloved Eixample wine bar and bistro steps from the hotel; enjoy a leisurely arrival lunch of charcuterie boards, pan con tomate, and a glass of Priorat red to ease into Barcelona time.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — two Michelin-starred avant-garde restaurant in Eixample; book the tasting menu for an extraordinary introduction to modern Catalan haute cuisine. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through your hotel concierge. Confirm Gaudí walking tour start time no earlier than 15:00 to allow comfortable check-in. Disfrutar requires reservations months ahead — confirm before travel.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell Sunrise Visit & Gràcia Brunch: Rise early for a private sunrise visit to Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park before the crowds arrive. Wander the mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room of coloured columns, and the sweeping panoramic terrace overlooking the city bathed in golden morning light. A personal guide narrates the utopian vision behind this UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Descend from the hills into the heart of Eixample for a skip-the-line private guided tour of Gaudí's magnum opus. Ascend the towers for breathtaking city views, explore the ethereal nave where light fractures into a kaleidoscope of colour, and visit the on-site museum to understand the basilica's century-long construction saga. Take time to linger in the tranquil surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Clubbing on Carrer de Parlament & Poble Sec: Begin the evening with craft cocktails at a chic rooftop bar in Poble Sec — try Bar Calders or a curated speakeasy recommended by your concierge. Move on to Carrer de Parlament's vibrant bar scene before heading to one of Barcelona's legendary clubs such as Sala Apolo or Paral·lel venues for a full premium nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast or a coffee and croissant at a local café near Park Güell in Gràcia neighbourhood before the sunrise visit.
meals.lunch: La Pepita (Gràcia) — a beautifully designed brunch spot in a former modernista pharmacy; enjoy smashed avocado toasts, artisan pastries, and fresh juices in an Instagram-worthy setting after your morning in the park.
meals.dinner: Tickets — Albert Adrià's acclaimed avant-garde tapas bar in Poble Sec; the perfect theatrical dinner before the nightlife crawl begins. Tasting portions of creative small plates in a circus-inspired space. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed-entry tickets for the Monumental Zone must be booked online in advance. Sunrise slot (around 07:00 in August) guarantees near-empty pathways. Wear comfortable shoes for both the park and Sagrada Família. Pace the evening — Barcelona clubs typically peak after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Late, leisurely morning to recover from nightlife. Enjoy a luxurious in-hotel breakfast followed by a private visit to Palau Güell — Gaudí's early masterpiece tucked in the Raval district. A guided tour reveals the extraordinary rooftop chimneys, the central hall with its parabolic dome, and the contrast between the ornate noble floors and the raw brick stables below.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Born & Waterfront Exploration: Stroll through the El Born neighbourhood, stopping at the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning example of Catalan Gothic architecture. Browse high-end concept stores and art galleries along Carrer del Rec. Head to the waterfront and board a private sailing charter for a 2-hour cruise along the Barcelona coastline, with chilled cava and tapas served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Cocktails & Fine Dining in Eixample: Return to the Eixample for sunset cocktails at the rooftop terrace of the Hotel Almanac or similar luxury rooftop with sweeping city views. Follow with dinner at a celebrated Eixample restaurant for a refined evening.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, artisan pastries, eggs prepared to order, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet (El Born) — a legendary cava bar serving house-poured sparkling wine with classic tapas: anchovies, olives, and house-made vermouth snacks in a beautifully tiled, atmospheric setting.
meals.dinner: Lasarte — three Michelin-starred restaurant by Martín Berasategui, located in Eixample; an unmissable pinnacle of Basque-Catalan fine dining with an exceptional wine cellar and impeccable service.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sailing charter through a luxury concierge service (e.g., Sailing Barcelona or similar); request chilled Moët or local cava on board. Lasarte is one of Spain's most decorated restaurants — reservations are essential and should be made months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe: Take a private car or cable car up to Montjuïc for a morning of architectural contrast. Visit the iconic Barcelona Pavilion — Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's 1929 masterpiece of modernist minimalism, with its reflecting pools, travertine walls, and Barcelona Chair originals. Continue to the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive Eixample Modernisme Deep Dive: Return to the neighbourhood for a private architectural tour focused on lesser-known Modernisme gems — Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and the interiors of the Palau del Baró de Quadras. End with a private visit inside the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau, Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking hospital complex and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Barcelona Nightlife — Premium Club Experience: Tonight, go deeper into Barcelona's legendary club scene. Your concierge arranges VIP table reservations at Pacha Barcelona or Opium Barcelona on the beachfront, or the more underground Razzmatazz for a multi-room music experience. Enjoy bottle service, private areas, and the electric energy of Barcelona after dark.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia (Gothic Quarter adjacent) or hotel breakfast — opt for a slow start with fresh pastries and café amb llet.
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet (Poble Sec) — a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for creative montaditos and an extraordinary tinned seafood selection; pair with house vermouth for an authentic Barcelona experience.
meals.dinner: Amar Barcelona (Hotel Arts, Barceloneta) — a Michelin-starred restaurant perched in the luxury beachfront hotel with panoramic sea views; contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with an emphasis on fresh seafood and local produce. Perfect pre-club dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) runs from Paral·lel metro or from the port — the port route offers spectacular views. VIP nightclub arrangements (guestlist, table bookings, transport) are best coordinated through your hotel concierge. Clubs open late — plan dinner for 21:00 and arrive at the club no earlier than 01:00.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Farewell Morning in Eixample: Sleep in and enjoy a final unhurried breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle walk along Passeig de Gràcia — Barcelona's grandest boulevard — for a last look at the Manzana de la Discordia (Block of Discord) and its competing Modernisme facades. Browse luxury boutiques: Loewe, Hermès, and local high-end designers are all located here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Architectural Photography Walk & Vermouth Hour: Arrange a final private guided photography walk with a local architectural photographer to capture the city's beauty through a professional lens — from Gaudí's facades to hidden Eixample courtyards. Conclude with a classic Barcelona vermouth hour (La Hora del Vermut) at a traditional bodega, savouring house vermouth, olives, and pan con tomate as a final ritual farewell to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation: A final celebratory dinner before preparing for departure (if flying the following day) or heading to the airport for a late flight. Pack, arrange private luxury transfer, and reflect on an extraordinary Barcelona experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy every detail of the hotel's morning service on your last day.
meals.lunch: Bar Calders (Poble Sec) or Cervecería Catalana (Eixample) — relaxed, quality Catalan lunch with patatas bravas, fresh seafood, and a glass of cold Estrella Damm or local white wine.
meals.dinner: Cinc Sentits — Michelin-starred tasting menu restaurant in Eixample celebrating the five senses through seasonal Catalan ingredients; an intimate, personal, and deeply memorable farewell dinner with an outstanding natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your departure is in the evening. The private photography walk can be booked through local agencies such as Foto Ruta or a concierge-recommended photographer. Cinc Sentits is an intimate restaurant — book the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for the full experience. Allow 45–60 minutes for airport transfer from Eixample.
